question: Will Frontier Group Holdings, Inc. file for bankruptcy protection before May 1, 2026?

forecasts.reference-class: US airline sector (ultra-low-cost carriers) with high leverage and cash-burn risk, using Frontier Group Holdings (ULCC) as a representative case

sources.claim: Metaculus forecasts a 9% probability that Frontier Group Holdings will file for bankruptcy protection before May 1, 2026.
ValueInvesting.io lists ULCC's probability of bankruptcy at about 45.74% over the next 24 months.
GuruFocus reports ULCC Altman Z-Score of 0.38, in the distress zone, implying bankruptcy risk within the next two years.
Frontier forecast a 2026 range for adjusted EPS from -$0.40 to +$0.50, with the midpoint around a $0.05 profit, signaling heavy emphasis on cost discipline rather than insolvency.
As of March 31, 2025, Frontier Group Holdings had no outstanding borrowings under its Revolving Loan Facility; debt maturities extend into 2026–2029, with no bankruptcy disclosure.
Frontier proposed merging with Spirit Airlines, which was in Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection at the time.
Spirit Airlines, in bankruptcy protection, rejected Frontier's renewed takeover bid.
Spirit Airlines filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in November 2024.
Spirit Airlines expects to exit Chapter 11 bankruptcy by summer 2026.
Frontier Airlines proposed merging with bankrupt Spirit Airlines in January 2025.
GAO: Since 2000, there have been dozens of airline bankruptcy filings; among large airlines with assets over $100 million, 24 occurred since 2000, with 12 after 2000.
Frontier Group reported a first-quarter loss, signaling ongoing financial stress but not bankruptcy.
Spirit bankruptcy developments provide sector distress context relevant to ULCC peers.
ULCC probability of bankruptcy is estimated at about 45.7% over the next 24 months by a market-model approach.

causal-factors.name: ULCC sector distress and high leverage
causal-factors.rationale: Industry-wide post-pandemic debt burdens and elevated cash burn raise bankruptcy risk for Frontier, reinforced by market-model estimates (e.g., ~46% over 24 months) and the Altman Z-score in distress.

causal-factors.name: Frontier liquidity and debt-maturity profile
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier reports no revolver borrowings as of 3/31/2025 with debt maturities into 2026–2029 and no bankruptcy disclosure, signaling resilience in the near term.

causal-factors.name: Spirit Airlines bankruptcy and consolidation risk
causal-factors.rationale: Spirit's Chapter 11 and Frontier's takeover talks introduce uncertainty but do not directly determine Frontier's near-term bankruptcy probability.

causal-factors.name: Public forecast anchors and base-rate signals
causal-factors.rationale: Metaculus around 9% and other anchor-based forecasts provide little directional pressure away from the anchor.

causal-factors.name: Altman Z-Score distress signal (ULCC)
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier Group Holdings ULCC has an Altman Z-Score of 0.37, which is in the distress zone and historically associated with higher bankruptcy risk within two years. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/term/zscore/ULCC

causal-factors.name: Strong liquidity and undrawn revolving facility
causal-factors.rationale: As of March 31, 2025 Frontier had no outstanding borrowings on its Revolving Loan Facility and about $889 million in total liquidity, supporting near term obligations and reducing bankruptcy risk. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1670076/000167007625000111/fron-20250331.htm

causal-factors.name: Near-term debt maturities pressures
causal-factors.rationale: Debt principal payments of 209 million in 2025 and 120 million in 2026 create near term obligations but are supported by ample liquidity including a large undrawn revolver. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1670076/000167007625000111/fron-20250331.htm

causal-factors.name: Spirit bankruptcy as sector distress signal
causal-factors.rationale: Spirit Airlines filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2024 and the ULCC sector faces ongoing restructuring, increasing industry tail risk for Frontier. Source: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2024/nov/18/spirit-airlines-files-bankruptcy-financial-losses

causal-factors.name: Market-based bankruptcy probability for ULCCs
causal-factors.rationale: ValueInvesting.io estimates Frontier ULCC bankruptcy probability at 45.74% over the next 24 months. Source: https://valueinvesting.io/ULCC/probability-of-bankruptcy

causal-factors.name: Frontier Spirit merger talks
causal-factors.rationale: Frontier has proposed merging with Spirit while Spirit was in bankruptcy; the outcome is uncertain and could either reduce risk via synergies or elevate risk via integration costs. Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/29/frontier-airlines-proposes-combining-spirit.html

causal-factors.name: GAO airline bankruptcy history context
causal-factors.rationale: GAO shows multiple airline bankruptcies since 2000, including several large carriers, indicating a nonzero baseline risk. Source: https://www.gao.gov/assets/a248035.html

causal-factors.name: Verizon acquisition closes and Frontier becomes part of Verizon
causal-factors.rationale: The transaction closed around January 20, 2026, eliminating Frontier as an independent entity and thereby removing Frontier's bankruptcy risk for the forecast horizon. Sources: turn8search0, turn8search1, turn8search2, turn8search5.

causal-factors.name: Regulatory approvals completed for the Verizon acquisition
causal-factors.rationale: All required regulatory clearances were obtained, clearing the path to closing and reducing bankruptcy risk associated with continued independent operations. Sources: turn8search1, turn8search0, turn8search2, turn8search5.

causal-factors.name: Frontier's pre-close liquidity and lack of near-term debt maturities
causal-factors.rationale: Public disclosures through 2025 showed substantial liquidity and no maturities before 2027, indicating low risk of imminent bankruptcy absent the Verizon deal; this supports a lower probability by May 1, 2026. Sources: turn8search3, turn6search4, turn6search5.

causal-factors.name: Spirit Airlines bankruptcy and ULCC sector distress context
causal-factors.rationale: Spirit’s Chapter 11 filings created sector distress for ULCC peers, but the Frontier-Verizon deal largely offsets Frontier-specific risk; net effect on Frontier’s odds remains minimal.

synthesis: The Verizon acquisition effectively eliminates Frontier's standalone bankruptcy risk within the forecast window. With the deal closing as described, the probability of filing before May 1, 2026 is essentially zero; only minor post-close integration risks could create a tiny tail risk.
